html:
The Battle of Agincourt was fought on 25 October 1415 near the village of Azincourt in northern France. A small, tired English army under King Henry V beat a much larger French one.

Henry had reopened the Hundred Years' War that summer by landing in Normandy and taking the port of Harfleur. Disease cost him many men. He then marched for English-held Calais, and the French army blocked his road. Henry had about 6,000 to 9,000 men, most of them archers. The French had perhaps two or three times as many, though historians disagree on the numbers. The field was a narrow strip of ploughed land between two woods. The French men-at-arms advanced on foot in heavy armour through deep mud, packed so tightly that they could hardly lift their weapons, while arrows fell on them from the sides. Thousands died, including much of the high nobility. Henry also had many prisoners killed when he feared a new attack.

Henry conquered Normandy in the following years. In 1420 the Treaty of Troyes made him heir to the crown of France. He died in 1422, and the tide turned against England at Orléans. Shakespeare made the battle famous.
